questions.question: Which of the following institute provide long-term credit to the farmers under cooperative credit structure in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Primary Land Development Banks**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The Primary Land Development Banks (also known as District Central Cooperative Banks or DCCBs) are key players in the cooperative credit structure in India, providing long-term credit facilities to farmers for development purposes.
 
• These banks provide credit for purposes like farm mechanization, minor irrigation, soil conservation, and other farm development programs.
 
• They play a crucial role in supporting and promoting agricultural and rural development in India.
 
• The District Central Cooperative Banks operate at the district level (hence their name) and are the link between rural areas and the state cooperative banks.
 
• They primarily finance the Primary Agricultural Credit Societies, which in turn lend money to individual farmers.
 
• It should be noted that the cooperative credit structure in India is three-tiered, consisting of:
 
 
• State Cooperative Banks (StCBs) at the state level
 
• District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) at the district level
 
• Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) at the village level
 
 
 
• These cooperative banks have played a pivotal role in meeting the credit requirements of the farmers in rural areas.

questions.question: Which of the following Vedas is also called "Book of Songs", "Veda of Mantras" or "Yoga of Songs"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Samveda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "Samveda" is an ancient Hindu text and one of the four main Vedas of Hinduism.

 It is a collection of tunes and chants, and is also called the "Book of Songs", the "Veda of Chants" or even the "Yoga of Songs".

 It is basically the words of "Rigveda" set to music.

 The Gandharvaveda deals with various aspects of Saundasau Ryashastra including art forms like music, dance, poetry, sculpture, erotica etc. It is related to the Samaveda.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rigveda:**

 
 
• The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas and one of the most important texts in the Hindu tradition.
 
• It is a large collection of hymns in praise of the deities, which are chanted in various rituals.
 
• Ayurveda is the Upaveda of Rigveda.
 
 
 
• **Atharvaveda:**
 
 
• The Atharvaveda is commonly referred to as the "Veda of magical formulas".
 
• All the routines of life are described in detail in this Veda.
 
• It consists of the three fundamental Upanishads – the Mundaka Upanishad, the Mandukya Upanishad and the Prasna Upanishad – and is known as the Veda of magical formulas.
 
 
 
• **Yajurveda:**
 
 
• The text in the Yajurveda ("worship knowledge" or "ritual knowledge") consists of ritual worship aphorisms, mantras and chants directly involved in worship services.
 
• Yajurveda was composed by Ved Vyas.​

questions.question: Deepa Sashindran, Raja Reddy and Radha Reddy are associated with which of the following Indian dances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• D**eepa Sashindra**n is a Kuchipudi dancer, and **Raja Reddy and Radha Reddy** are famous Kuchipudi exponents.
 
• **Deepa Sashindran**:
 
 
• A Kuchipudi dancer and **choreographer who has performed in India and abroad**.
 
• She has created original works, including solo performances, dance dramas, and features.
 
• She has also taught workshops and performed in Doha, Dubai, and Abu Dhabi.
 
 
 
• Raja and Radha Reddy are Indian Kuchipudi dancing couples, gurus, and choreographers.
 
• They are renowned as exponents of the south Indian dance form of Kuchipudi.
 
• Their names are synonymous with Kuchipudi dance and are regarded solely responsible for bringing it on the cultural map of the world.
 
• For their services to the field of arts, the Government of India has conferred on them the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan awards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Kuchipudi:

 
 
• Kuchipudi is a major classical dance form of India that originated in a village of the Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Kuchipudi involves different foot movements and is generally a team performance.
 
• The central them of Kuchipudi is Bhagavata puran.
 
• The dancers of Kuchipudi came to be known as Bhagavathalus.
 
 
 
• Bharatnatyam:
 
 
• Bharatanatyam is the oldest and major classical dance form of India that originated in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It traces its origins back to the Natyashastra, ancient treaties on theatre written by the mythic priest Bharata.
 
 
 
• Kathakali:
 
 
• Kathakali is a classical Indian dance form which is a story play genre of art and is the folk dance form of Kerala.
 
• It is a 'story play' genre of art, but one distinguished by the elaborately colorful make-up, costumes, and face masks that the traditionally male actor-dancers wear.

questions.question: Who among the following opposed Mahatma Gandhi's association with the Khilafat movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohammed Ali Jinnah**__.

__
 
• **While Jinnah was away in England, Gandhi changed his tactics and united Hindus and Muslims by espousing a Muslim-only religious cause: the ‘Khilafat**’.
 
• Jinnah was especially opposed to befriending radical Muslim leaders and felt it would be nothing short of a `disaster for the country.
 
 
• The** Khilafat movement**, a campaign that called for the restoration of a caliphate **spread across several countries, had started in 1919.**
 
• It had gained traction in India only after **Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi** had fused the pan-Islamic agitation with the **Non-Cooperation Movement.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan**, also known as **Badshah Khan, Frontier Gandhi, or Bacha Khan**, and honorably addressed as **Fakhr-e-Afghan, was a Pashtun freedom fighter and independence activist against British colonial rule** in India. 
 
• **Abul Kasem Fazlul Huq **popularly known as **Sher-e-Bangla (Lion of Bengal) **was a **British Indian and Pakistani lawyer**, writer, and statesman from eastern Bengal (present-day Bangladesh). 
 
• **Abul Kalam Ghulam Muhiyuddin Ahmed bin Khairuddin Al-Hussaini Azad** was an **Indian independence activist, Islamic theologian, writer, and senior leader of the Indian National Congress.**

questions.question: When did the Indian Government launch the Digital India program to connect rural areas with high-speed Internet networks and improve digital literacy?

• The Digital India campaign was initiated by the Indian Government to make government services accessible to people electronically by improving online infrastructure and improving internet connectivity.
 
• It was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 1st July 2015.

• 
 With a vision of inclusive growth in the areas of electronic services, goods, manufacturing, and job opportunities, Digital India was established.

• **To provide universal access to high-speed internet connectivity in all parts of the country.**
 
• **To transform government services into digital platforms for efficient and transparent delivery.**
 
• **To empower citizens through digital literacy programs and access to digital resources.**
 
• **To ensure easy availability of government information and services to citizens electronically.**
 
• **To promote domestic manufacturing of electronic goods and create job opportunities in the electronics industry.**
 
• **To provide skill development programs and promote the growth of the IT and IT-enabled services sector.**

questions.question: The strong, gusty, hot, dry winds blowing during the day over the north and northwestern India are called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Loo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Loo** is a strong, gusty, hot, dry wind that blows during the day in the summer season.
 
• It is prevalent over the north and northwestern parts of India and Pakistan.
 
• The temperature of the Loo can reach up to 45-50 degrees Celsius, making it extremely dangerous and potentially fatal to humans and animals.
 
• The Loo wind is a significant weather phenomenon in these regions, known for its ability to cause heat strokes and dehydration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Foehn**

 
 
• A Foehn is a type of dry, warm, down-slope wind that occurs in the lee (downwind side) of a mountain range.
 
• It is associated with the rapid warming and drying of air masses as they descend mountain slopes.
 
• This phenomenon is common in the Alps and other mountainous regions.
 
 
 
• **Khamsin**
 
 
• Khamsin is a dry, hot, sandy wind blowing from the south, usually occurring in Egypt and the eastern Mediterranean region.
 
• It typically occurs in late winter and early spring and can raise temperatures significantly.
 
 
 
• **Sirocco**
 
 
• Sirocco is a Mediterranean wind that comes from the Sahara and can reach hurricane speeds in North Africa and Southern Europe.
 
• It is known for carrying large amounts of dust and sand from the desert into the Mediterranean regions.

questions.question: What is the process in which a thick oxide layer of aluminium is developed over the aluminium articles that is dyed to give an attractive finish?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Anodising**__**.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anodising** is the process in which a thick oxide layer of aluminium is developed over the aluminium articles that is dyed to give an attractive finish.
 
• **Aluminium anodising** is a process that creates a layer of aluminium oxide to protect the base metal from environmental impacts.
 
• **What is Anodising?**
 
 
• It is an electrochemical process that develops an aluminium oxide coat on the surface of the part or product. 
 
• This protects the product from wear and tear while improving the aesthetics. In this process, the product to be coated acts as an anode in an electrolytic cell, hence the name.
 
 
 
• On an industrial scale, anodising made its first appearance in **1923**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Aluminium is the** second most** widely used metal in the world.
 
• Engineers prefer aluminium for its** light weight**, corrosion resistance and reasonable price.
 
• However, untreated aluminium has** low wear resistance**.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an objective of the Monetary Policy of Reserve Bank of India?

options.text: Increase growth rate of the country
Flow of credit to the priority sector of the economy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Reducing fiscal deficit**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Monetary policy** is the procedure by which the monetary authority of a nation, normally the central bank or currency board, controls either the expense of short-term borrowing or the cash supply, focusing on inflation or the loan fee to guarantee value strength and general trust in the currency.
 
• 
 Developing the Monetary Policy in India is a prerogative of the Reserve Bank of India. Hence, it is also called the **Monetary Policy of RBI**. The RBI is vested with this responsibility under the **RBI Act, 1934**. The Monetary policy of RBI regulates the money supply, availability of credit and interest rates.
 
 
• 
 The main objectives of the RBI's ____Monetary Policy in India are__:

 
 
• 
 To regulate money supply in the economy
 
 
• 
 To attain **price stability**
 
 
• 
 To promote **economic growth**
 
 
• 
 To promote saving and investment
 
 
• 
 To control business cycles
 
 
• 
 To promote exports and substitute imports
 
 
• 
 To develop infrastructure
 
 
• 
 To regulate and expand banking
 
 
• 
 To **ensure more credit for priority sector**
 
 
• 
 To promote employment
 
 
• 
 To manage aggregate demand
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__**

 
• 
 
 In India, the **government manages its fiscal deficit** by borrowing from various sources like the Reserve Bank of India, public sector banks, large public institutions, overseas markets, capital markets, and it can raise funds from the public as well.

 

**Based on the above discussion we can conclude that, reducing fiscal deficit is not an objective of the Monetary Policy of Reserve Bank of India.**

questions.question: Which portal was launched by Shri Piyush Goyal to improve the business environment and track suggestions for improvement?

options.text: Ease of Doing Business & Regulatory Affairs portal

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ease of Doing Business (EoDB) and Regulatory Affairs portal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Shri Piyush Goyal launched the CII Ease of Doing Business (EoDB) and Regulatory Affairs portal to enhance transparency and accountability in India's business environment.**
 
• The portal aims to track progress, submissions, and updates on Ease of Doing Business initiatives by the government and CII.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The portal includes a member dashboard for real-time tracking and ensuring meaningful resolution of concerns.
 
• Shri Goyal emphasized the importance of technological upgrades to improve the efficiency of State and Central government portals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• CII Ease of Doing Business (EoDB) and Regulatory Affairs Portal__

 __
 
• The portal is designed to offer insights into India’s business environment and help receive and track suggestions for improving the Ease of Doing Business.
 
• The portal also facilitates the National Single Window System (NSWS) to guide investors in applying for business-related approvals.
 
 
 
• Shri Piyush Goyal’s Vision__
 
 
• The Minister emphasized the need for a cooperative federalism approach and the importance of feedback from industry stakeholders to improve business processes.
 
• He urged stakeholders to work faster and harder to make India the third-largest economy in the next three years.
